AknSource.description:
One upstream that yields documents convertible to AKN.

Distinct from `SourceAdapter`, the acquisition substrate keyed by adapter kind:
this is a format-and-protocol pairing declared in `config.json#akn_sources`.
Both coexist during the schema migration and `effective_tier` walks both; legacy
configs without `format`/`protocol` default to PDF over HTTP.

description.description: Free-text, these configs were hand-written before the structured shape landed and frequently carry narrative provenance.
description.title: Description

requires_token.description: Token-gated source: skip in `effective_tier` when the env var is unset unless `fallback_format` declares a usable downgrade.
requires_token.title: Requires Token

AknSource.title: AknSource

amending_body_structure.description: Body shape of an amending instrument. `two_pasal_roman`: the host's own articles are Roman, so an Arabic-numbered one after them is quoted text.
amending_body_structure.title: Amending Body Structure

amendment_item_kind.description: Hierarchy element that numbers one amendment made by an amending article (a numbered `Angka` item). What follows it belongs to the amended statute, so it must not compete in the host's numbering. Empty leaves the pass inert.
amendment_item_kind.title: Amendment Item Kind

trigger_phrases.description: Lead-in phrases marking an embedded amendment article: a number following one of these plus a colon is quoted content, not a new top-level article.
trigger_phrases.title: Trigger Phrases

AttachmentCaption.description:
A caption line opening an attachment. AKN models a schedule and a
mandatory companion alike, so legal force is declared per caption.

always_opens.description: True where no table in the body carries this caption, so a line that opens with it always begins the attachment.
always_opens.title: Always Opens

caption.description: Centred in the source, so the match tolerates a wide indent.
caption.title: Caption

hierarchy.description: Levels the attachment's own content uses: an annex can be a lettered outline rather than the article hierarchy of the body it is attached to. Empty keeps today's behaviour: the body's levels, or none.
hierarchy.title: Hierarchy

normative.description: False for an explanatory memorandum: no norm, and no legal basis.
normative.title: Normative

prefix.description: True where the caption opens a longer title on the same line ("SCHEDULE of fees…"), so the caption need only begin the line. The line is the heading.
prefix.title: Prefix

AttachmentCaption.title: AttachmentCaption

BindingRegime.description:
Non-membership binding regime, treaty frameworks, bilateral regimes,
constitutional annexes. Used for instruments that are legally binding on a
jurisdiction but are not memberships in an international organisation.

territories.description: Territorial / temporal scope, typically populated for SC resolutions and other time-bounded regimes; absent on permanent treaty frameworks.
territories.title: Territories

BindingRegime.title: BindingRegime

CalendarConversion.description:
Deterministic conversion rule for non-Gregorian local calendars.

kind selects which optional fields apply:

- epoch_offset  single-epoch calendars. Gregorian = local_year + epoch_year,
                where epoch_year is an integer offset (Buddhist Era -543).
- era_table     named era segments with boundaries.
- hijri_lunar   Lunar calendar, ~354 days. Needs codify.calendar, not an offset.
- hijri_solar   Solar calendar, Gregorian year length.
- ethiopian     ~7-8 year offset, 13-month year.
- buddhist      Buddhist Era calendar, epoch_year -543.
- bikram_samvat 57-year offset, month-sensitive (Chaitra straddles the
                mid-April new year).

date_cues.description: Phrases that introduce the date a document was made. A dated line elsewhere in the text is some other instrument's.
date_cues.title: Date Cues

epoch_year.description: Integer added to the local year to give the Gregorian year (Buddhist -543, ROC and Juche 1911, since their year 1 is 1912 CE). None for calendars without a simple offset: hijri, ethiopian, era_table, bikram_samvat.
epoch_year.title: Epoch Year

month_day_is_gregorian.description: Whether the months and days coincide with the Gregorian ones, so only the year converts. False for any calendar with a grid of its own.
month_day_is_gregorian.title: Month Day Is Gregorian

month_names.description: Month names in the local calendar's own order, index 0 = month 1. Present only where a dated line is read off the source text.
month_names.title: Month Names

new_year_month.description: Month-sensitive conversions (Bikram Samvat New Year mid-April).
new_year_month.title: New Year Month

new_year_reform_year.description: The local year began in this month before `new_year_reform_year`, so an earlier date carries the previous year's number and the offset is short.
new_year_reform_year.title: New Year Reform Year

offset.description: Offset variant for month-sensitive: subtract `offset` from local year before the new-year day, otherwise `offset + 1`.
offset.title: Offset

year_particles.description: Words marking a year as belonging to this calendar ("B.E.", "A.H.").
year_particles.title: Year Particles

CalendarConversion.title: CalendarConversion

ClassificationRule.description:
Deterministic rule for assigning a document class from the incoming header or
metadata. Tried in descending priority; the first match wins. No match falls back to
`default_document_class` and to whatever heuristics `StructuringConfig.prompt_additions`
still carries.

signal          what `pattern` is tested against
  date_range      nothing; the match is `date_from`/`date_until` alone, for laws
                  post-dating a regime change
  preamble_match  the preamble or enacting-formula text
  issuer_role     the enacting body's role (for example a head of state or a cabinet)
  gazette_series  the official gazette series the document was published in
  title_regex     the document title (a fixed prefix such as "Regulation:")
ClassificationRule.title: ClassificationRule

output.description: basket path, relative to repo root
output.title: Output

DiscoveryConfig.title: DiscoveryConfig

amendment_markers.description: The pair a publisher prints around amended words; brackets are only the commonest. A list because a tuple crosses the schema boundary as unknown.
amendment_markers.title: Amendment Markers

authoritative_language.description: Per-class authoritative language, falling back to the jurisdiction's when None. Vatican needs it: Latin for canon law, Italian for the City State.
authoritative_language.title: Authoritative Language

extends.description: Another class of this jurisdiction whose fields this one lays over. One level.
extends.title: Extends

number_has_year_prefix.description: A matching year prefix in the printed serial is separate from the URI number.
number_has_year_prefix.title: Number Has Year Prefix

number_source.description: "title_identity": the URI number is always the title digest, never a stated serial, for classes whose serials repeat across issuers.
number_source.title: Number Source

search_rank.description: Where this class sits in the legal hierarchy, for ranking a name search: higher outranks lower on a close title match. Unset means no weighting, so a jurisdiction whose hierarchy nobody has transcribed keeps pure relevance order. Ranks: 4 constitutional, 3 primary legislation, 2 executive decree, 1 subordinate regulation or decision, 0 implementing instructions.
search_rank.title: Search Rank

short_label.description: Compact display form (e.g. "VKM" for al/vendim). Falls back to the title-cased doctype when unset. Single source of truth for the UI + PDF.
short_label.title: Short Label

DocumentPlacedTable.description:
A table outside every provision, with the eIds it sits under (outermost
first) so a reader can place it and a subtree read can keep it.
DocumentPlacedTable.title: DocumentPlacedTable

DocumentProvision.title: DocumentProvision

DocumentProvisionBlock.description:
One row in a nested-provision tree (paragraph / subparagraph / …).

Carries its own number, optional heading, intro inline run, nested
blocks, and trailing wrap-up so renderers can present a hanging
numbered hierarchy rather than a flattened paragraph. `table` is set
(and everything else empty) when `akn_type == "table"`.
DocumentProvisionBlock.title: DocumentProvisionBlock

DocumentSection.description:
Hierarchical container, title / chapter / part / article / etc.

Holds child sections and provisions in their persisted `position` order.
Top-level provisions (those without an enclosing section) hang off the
`VersionDocument.provisions` list instead.
DocumentSection.title: DocumentSection

DocumentTable.description: An AKN `<table>`, eId-keyed like every other citable unit.
DocumentTable.title: DocumentTable

DocumentTableCell.description:
One `<th>`/`<td>`; `content` is the same inline AST as any other cell of
legal text, so refs/terms/citations inside a table cell still render.
DocumentTableCell.title: DocumentTableCell

calendar_conversion.description: Structured conversion rule. Populated for non-Gregorian jurisdictions (NP, TW, KP, JP, IR, ET, TH). FRBR URIs always use Gregorian (ADR 001), this drives the conversion utility.

title_identity.description: Declared where instruments carry no number and the title is the identity.

captions.description: The closed caption vocabulary a `caption` level answers to.
captions.title: Captions

eid_abbrev.description: Overrides the element's canonical eId prefix. Set it only where the element cannot imply one (hcontainer: sch, xhd; two local terms on one element) or the publisher's own AKN differs (UK SIs number sections reg_N).
eid_abbrev.title: Eid Abbrev

local_terms.description: Unified multilingual store for local_term_ara / local_script_rus / etc. Keys are ISO 639-3 language codes or "script:<iso-15924>".
local_terms.title: Local Terms

marker_form.description: Genres whose levels carry no keyword: a judgment writes "DUDUK PERKARA" and "[1.1]", never its hierarchy term. Unset keeps keyword matching.
marker_form.title: Marker Form

InlineAnchor.description: Running text a citation can name, such as a recital.
InlineAnchor.title: InlineAnchor

InlineNote.description: A footnote bound to the provision it annotates, not part of its prose.
InlineNote.title: InlineNote

adoption_markers.description: Phrases declaring the instrument adopts another body's numbered text, which every count over the document must read as an attachment, not its own structure.
adoption_markers.title: Adoption Markers

akn_sources.description: Legacy / hand-curated list of upstreams. Coexists with `source_adapters` during the schema-migration window; `effective_tier` walks both.
akn_sources.title: Akn Sources

attachments.description: Captions opening an attachment, whose numbering restarts the body's.
attachments.title: Attachments

binding_regimes.description: Non-membership binding regimes (treaty frameworks, bilateral regimes, constitutional annexes), which are not memberships.
binding_regimes.title: Binding Regimes

closing_phrases.description: `LegalEra.closing_phrases` for a jurisdiction that declares no eras. An era's own list wins where it declares one.
closing_phrases.title: Closing Phrases

effective_tier.description:
Tier actually achievable in the current environment.

Walks both `source_adapters` and the legacy `akn_sources`, taking the best
(lowest) tier. Token-gated entries with an unset env var are skipped unless the
source declares a `fallback_format`, whose tier contributes instead.
effective_tier.title: Effective Tier

enacting_formula_markers.description: Evidence the source carries its own formula, so no fallback is injected. Never a cut point: a phrase here may open the instrument, not close it.
enacting_formula_markers.title: Enacting Formula Markers

footnote_markers.description: `LegalEra.footnote_markers` for a jurisdiction that declares no eras. An era's own list wins where it declares one.
footnote_markers.title: Footnote Markers

furniture_inline_patterns.description: Furniture that shares a line with real content, so whole-line disposal would take the content with it: a portal credit run, a stamped URL. Narrower than `ocr_header_patterns`, which also matches the real title on page one.
furniture_inline_patterns.title: Furniture Inline Patterns

furniture_line_patterns.description: Furniture whose whole line is disposable: mastheads, page numbers, stamps. Narrower than `ocr_header_patterns`, which also carries the running title and so matches the real title on page one. Substring scrubbing is safe for both sets, whole-line disposal only for this one.
furniture_line_patterns.title: Furniture Line Patterns

legal_eras.description: Drafting periods, for reporting quality per era rather than per corpus. Empty means one undivided population. Distinct from `CalendarRule.eras`, which is a regnal year table.
legal_eras.title: Legal Eras

lexicon_words.description: Legal vocabulary particular to this jurisdiction, folded into the language's word list when a page is scored. A term naming one jurisdiction is that jurisdiction's data, not the language's.
lexicon_words.title: Lexicon Words

min_anchor_coverage.description: Minimum ratio of captured anchors over marker literals in the source. Ingest fails below it, so a silently-partial AKN cannot ship. 0.80 tolerates in-prose cross-references without over-firing. 0.0 disables.
min_anchor_coverage.title: Min Anchor Coverage

name_translations.description: ISO-639-3 language code → localised jurisdiction name. Used by the PDF exporter to render the cover in the target language without a hardcoded Python map. Mirror of `Law.title_translations`.
name_translations.title: Name Translations

note.description: Free-text note at the jurisdiction level for cross-cutting guidance.
note.title: Note

ocr_header_patterns.description:
Running header and footer text that leaks into article bodies during OCR. Stripped from `

` before translation so the LLM never sees it. Literal regex strings, so a profile author adds patterns without touching Python.
ocr_header_patterns.title: Ocr Header Patterns

opening_material_terminators.description: Phrases the recitals precede, after which pre-body text is page bleed.
opening_material_terminators.title: Opening Material Terminators

placeholders.description: Whole-string markers for missing or struck content, beyond the platform default.
placeholders.title: Placeholders

pool_excluded_refers_to.description: `refersTo` values marking a duty on someone other than the instrument's subjects: units at or under a marked element stay readable but leave the pool.
pool_excluded_refers_to.title: Pool Excluded Refers To

public_reference.description: Ships in the open core. Defaults False, so a jurisdiction joins the open set by a deliberate edit: excluded by default rather than included and simplified, because a simplified config is still a tell about what was studied.
public_reference.title: Public Reference

residual_legal_systems.description: Foreign corpora still residually applicable here: pre-independence or occupying-power law left in force, VA for suppletive Italian law, and so on. Enables amendment/consolidation agents to traverse layered systems.
residual_legal_systems.title: Residual Legal Systems

segmentation.description: Where one source holds several instruments, how their openings are read.

source_truncation_floor.description: Share of a document's contents listing that may lack a body before the source is read as truncated. Off by default: the separating value was measured on the corpora that declare it, and a partial corpus cannot evidence a threshold for a series it has never seen. 0.0 disables.
source_truncation_floor.title: Source Truncation Floor

synthetic.description: Fictional jurisdictions authored as synthetic test material (the AKN-spine scan factory). Discovered and validated like any other config, but kept out of the derived registry and the world atlas, which are real-only.
synthetic.title: Synthetic

tier.description: Promoted from registry.json, which is derived rather than maintained. Ladder: 1 AKN native, 2 XML-structured, 3 HTML anchors, 4 PDF-only, 5 no online statute base.
tier.title: Tier

LawSummary.description: The listing row, without the hosted platform's lens and translation fields.
LawSummary.title: LawSummary

LegalEra.description:
A period whose documents share a drafting convention and authority.

Structural quality tracks era more than jurisdiction, so it is reported per era.
``from_``/``to`` are inclusive ISO dates, either may be open, and the field is
spelled ``from`` in the config files.

authority_patterns.description: How this era's offices are named in provision text. Review candidates, not verdicts: a match says the office is named, not that the provision grants it a power, since the same name appears in signature blocks and definitions. Opt-in per era, because an era ending is not its authority being abolished.
authority_patterns.title: Authority Patterns

calendar.description: The calendar this era's instruments are dated in, where it differs from the jurisdiction's current one. None means it does not differ. Same closed set as the jurisdiction's own field, so the two cannot drift apart.
calendar.title: Calendar

closing_phrases.description: Phrases opening the attestation that closes a document of this era, so the promulgation and signature stop being read as the last article's text. Era-scoped because the wording follows the enacting authority.
closing_phrases.title: Closing Phrases

footnote_markers.description: Regex for how a footnote marker opens in this era. The modern set uses superscripts and the older ones a parenthesised numeral; declaring only one form silently drops the other era.
footnote_markers.title: Footnote Markers

LegalEra.title: LegalEra

citations.description: Per-instrument citation map, absorbs si_citation / decree_citation / loi_citation / law_citation / ordonnance_citation etc. without a separate field per jurisdiction.
citations.title: Citations

numbers_unique_across_years.description: Whether an instrument number identifies a work on its own. False almost everywhere: most jurisdictions restart numbering each year, so a citation that omits its date names one of many. Declaring it true lets a year-less citation resolve on the number, and is a claim about the whole series rather than about the corpus held, which may hold only one of the collisions and so cannot disprove it.
numbers_unique_across_years.title: Numbers Unique Across Years

series_citation_connectors.description: Regex fragments that may sit between a series name and its number.
series_citation_connectors.title: Series Citation Connectors

series_citations.description: Instruments cited by a never-reused series number and no year. Order matters: full names before abbreviations, so the full form wraps first.
series_citations.title: Series Citations

PlaceholderMarker.description:
A whole-string pattern a publisher writes where content is missing or
struck, and the AKN status the unit should carry for it.
PlaceholderMarker.title: PlaceholderMarker

PlaceholderStatus.description:
The AKN `@status` a placeholder unit should carry; named so the generated
contract keeps a stable alias rather than a numbered `Status`.
PlaceholderStatus.title: PlaceholderStatus

ResidualLaw.description:
Another jurisdiction's corpus that is still residually applicable here.

Used for layered legal systems where historical residual law, law inherited
from a predecessor legal order, or foreign law continues in force alongside
native legislation. Examples:
  - another jurisdiction's law applied as a suppletive source.
  - a historical codification still applied to general private law.
  - an inherited common law (but usually too embedded to carve out as
        discrete residuals).

`source_jurisdiction` is a Codify code that must resolve to an existing
config. Downstream consolidation/amendment agents can traverse these to
find the source corpus.

superseded_by.description: Superseding acts (as FRBR URIs or free-text citations).
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

ResidualLaw.title: ResidualLaw

SegmentationConfig.description:
Lines that open an issue or an act, for telling apart the instruments one
source holds. Absent means the jurisdiction declares none, and nothing splits.

act_heading_patterns.description: Regexes matched at a line start; a `number` group, where present, is the label.
act_heading_patterns.title: Act Heading Patterns

contents_keywords.description: Headings of a contents listing, matched case-insensitively at a line start.
contents_keywords.title: Contents Keywords

issue_heading_patterns.description: The level above acts: a gazette issue within a bound volume.
issue_heading_patterns.title: Issue Heading Patterns

printed_page_pattern.description: A printed page number in a page's furniture; its first participating group is the number.
printed_page_pattern.title: Printed Page Pattern

skip_heading_patterns.description: Headings of instruments that are not acts (notices, appointments): kept apart, not ingested.
skip_heading_patterns.title: Skip Heading Patterns

trailing_section_patterns.description: Whole lines opening a trailing section never ingested: no engine reads from there on.
trailing_section_patterns.title: Trailing Section Patterns

SegmentationConfig.title: SegmentationConfig

SeriesCitation.description: A citation naming an instrument by series number alone ("Act No. 386").

name.description: Regex for the instrument's name or abbreviation, matched case-insensitively.
name.title: Name

SeriesCitation.title: SeriesCitation

SourceAdapter.description:
One upstream portal for this jurisdiction; multiple permitted.

url_template placeholders: {country} {doctype} {year} {number} {frbr_uri}. Auth
tokens resolve from the env var named by auth_env_var, never stored here.

parser.description: Names a registered structured parser (codify.pipeline.parsers) that converts this adapter's primary body deterministically; None -> the universal structuring lane.
parser.title: Parser

SourceAdapter.title: SourceAdapter

body_opens_with_container.description: True where the drafting standard puts every article inside a container, so an article before the first one is a citation in the opening material. Some laws cite the constitution that way in the legal-basis recital.
body_opens_with_container.title: Body Opens With Container

citation_articles.description: Articles that may sit between the clause and the name (`the`). Language data: most languages have none, and no article is assumed.
citation_articles.title: Citation Articles

citation_lead_ins.description: Phrases introducing a law's own short name (`may be cited as`), the common-law short-title device.
citation_lead_ins.title: Citation Lead Ins

citation_subjects.description: How an instrument refers to itself when it declares its short name (`This Act`). Required alongside `citation_lead_ins`: the same phrasing names the schools and offices a law creates, so an unanchored clause takes the school's name for the law's.
citation_subjects.title: Citation Subjects

citation_successors.description: Words that, following a marker's number on its own line, make the line a citation list rather than a provision ("Article 5 to Article 9 apply").
citation_successors.title: Citation Successors

classification_rules.description: Deterministic classification rules, evaluated by descending priority before the AI prompt. prompt_additions keeps tacit style hints only.
classification_rules.title: Classification Rules

designation_rule.description: Derives a short name from the title's own grammar where the tradition declares no short title. EU acts are cited by form and number.
designation_rule.title: Designation Rule

example_markers.description: Lead-ins that introduce specimen legislation in a drafting manual (`Contoh`), whose markers are displayed rather than enacted.
example_markers.title: Example Markers

insertion_suffixes.description: Words after a marker's number that mark an inserted unit ("5 bis"), mapped to the eId form. One shared table, like `ordinal_words`: never blank, a number, or a bare Latin letter.
insertion_suffixes.title: Insertion Suffixes

long_title_lead_ins.description: Openings of the document's own long title (`An Act`), marked up as `<longTitle>` so the official title comes from the text rather than from a filename.
long_title_lead_ins.title: Long Title Lead Ins

marker_boundary.description: `line_anchored` where the drafting standard puts the marker on its own line and the sources keep it, so a mid-sentence citation cannot anchor.
marker_boundary.title: Marker Boundary

marker_order.description: `number_first` where the number precedes the keyword ("15. §", "I. FEJEZET").
marker_order.title: Marker Order

marker_tolerances.description: OCR damage the sources carry, tolerated for this jurisdiction only and byte-identical elsewhere. `missing_separator` is "Pasal24".
marker_tolerances.title: Marker Tolerances

ordinal_words.description: Ordinal words used as container numbers ("Bagian Kesatu" is part 1). Declared in the source's own casing; matching is case-sensitive.
ordinal_words.title: Ordinal Words

prose_precursors.description: Words ending the previous line when a citation wraps onto the next, which a boundary rule cannot see. Empty falls back to the script pack's list.
prose_precursors.title: Prose Precursors

recurring_furniture.description: True where the layout engine files footnotes and page-top captions under header or footer: furniture is then only what repeats, and a block opening on a marker is a note.
recurring_furniture.title: Recurring Furniture

reference_nouns.description: Words that introduce a citation's number ("Pasal 41 ayat (3)"). A line ending in one of these makes the bracketed number on the next line part of the citation, not a structural marker opening a new provision.
reference_nouns.title: Reference Nouns

sameline_precursors.description: Precursors that mark a citation only when adjacent on the same line.
sameline_precursors.title: Sameline Precursors

direct_effect.description: Effect spectrum, from strongest (override) to weakest (none). Legacy bool values are coerced to `"direct"`/`"none"` at load time.
direct_effect.title: Direct Effect

member_since.description: Loose string, year-only values like "1999" appear in corpus.
member_since.title: Member Since

member_until.description: Only set when status is "former". ISO 8601.
member_until.title: Member Until

protocol_references.description: Structured but free, the treaty/protocol that creates the carve-out. Examples: "Protocol 21 TFEU", "Protocol 10 Act of Accession 2003", "Edinburgh Agreement 1992", "Withdrawal Agreement 2020".
protocol_references.title: Protocol References

rejoined_on.description: Reactivation date, for the Morocco → AU 2017 pattern (original member_since is 1963, AU left 1984, rejoined_on 2017-01-30).
rejoined_on.title: Rejoined On

suspension_periods.description: History of suspension / reinstatement pairs. Use for Fiji-style cycles and for jurisdictions currently suspended (with suspended_until=None).
suspension_periods.title: Suspension Periods

transposition_required.description: Some configs use a bool; others list the specific instrument types that require transposition (e.g., ["directive"]).
transposition_required.title: Transposition Required

SuspensionPeriod.description:
One period of suspension from a supranational body.

Used inside `SupranationalMembership.suspension_periods` to record the
start and (optional) end of a suspension, plus its scope. A list is the
right shape because a jurisdiction can cycle through multiple suspensions.

scope.description: Suspension scopes observed in practice: full rights withdrawal vs. technocratic carve-outs (no decision-making, no voting, expelled from meetings only). Default is the worst case.
scope.title: Scope

SuspensionPeriod.title: SuspensionPeriod

eId.description: NCName-compatible, permitting camelCase and hyphenated forms both seen in the corpus. min_length=1 keeps the empty alias from raising an opaque pattern-mismatch.
eId.title: Eid

TitleIdentity.description:
How a jurisdiction that numbers nothing derives an identity from a title.
Every field is a literal `codify.frbr.identity_from_title` reads.

consolidation_markers.description: Parenthetical words marking a re-publication; an edition number after one is the edition folded in, not this document's.
consolidation_markers.title: Consolidation Markers

edition_markers.description: Words inside a parenthetical naming this instrument's edition, spelling variants included; the first is canonical and is what a slug carries.
edition_markers.title: Edition Markers

strip_prefixes.description: Document-kind words opening a short title, longest first.
strip_prefixes.title: Strip Prefixes

year_particles.description: Words marking the year that follows as the instrument's own.
year_particles.title: Year Particles

TitleIdentity.title: TitleIdentity

laws_africa_reference.description: Some configs use a URL string, others a bool flag ("does laws.africa cover this?").
laws_africa_reference.title: Laws Africa Reference

VersionDocument.description: Full body of a single version, rendered as a tree.
VersionDocument.title: VersionDocument

get.description: The version as the reader's section tree, not as AKN.
